before.stem: Let H_t denote past states, controls and measurements in the lecture’s model. Which pair preserves both conditional-independence assumptions?

options.text: p(x_t | H_t) = p(x_t | x_(t−1)); p(z_t | H_t,x_t) = p(z_t | x_t), dropping the current control from motion.
p(x_t | H_t) = p(x_t | x_(t−1),u_t); p(z_t | H_t,x_t) = p(z_t), dropping dependence on the current state.
p(x_t | H_t) = p(x_t | x_(t−1),u_t); p(z_t | H_t,x_t) = p(z_t | x_t).
p(x_t | H_t) = p(x_t | x_(t−1),u_t); p(z_t | H_t,x_t) = p(z_t | x_(t−1)), using only the previous state for sensing.

citations.locator: Lecture L44, physical PDF page 1384, printed footer 15: Measurement conditional independence versus transition
citations.evidenceText:
State Completeness & Markov Assumption

•  A state 𝒙𝒕​ is complete if it fully describes the system at time 𝑡, so past states
   𝒙𝟎:𝒕−𝟏, measurements 𝒛𝟏:𝒕−𝟏, or controls 𝒖𝟏:𝒕 provide no additional information
   for predicting the future.
•  Such temporal processes are known as Markov chains,
   defined by the Markov property and its two key
   conditional independence assumptions.
   – State Transition model: Probability of present state 𝒙𝒕 ​depends only on the
       previous state 𝒙𝒕−𝟏​ and current control 𝒖𝒕​.
               𝑝𝒙𝒕𝒙𝟎:𝒕−𝟏, 𝒛𝟏:𝒕−𝟏, 𝒖𝟏:𝒕= 𝑝𝒙𝒕𝒙𝒕−𝟏, 𝒖𝒕
   – Measurement model: Present measurement 𝒛𝒕
      depends only on the current state.
                   𝑝𝒛𝒕𝒙𝟎:𝒕, 𝒛𝟏:𝒕−𝟏, 𝒖𝟏:𝒕= 𝑝𝒛𝒕𝒙𝒕

solution.justification: A sufficient current state screens the present measurement from history; the transition instead uses the previous state together with the current control.

optionExplanations.o1: The controlled transition retains the current input u_t.
optionExplanations.o2: Conditional independence from history given x_t does not imply unconditional independence from x_t.
optionExplanations.o3: Motion is conditioned on the previous state and current control; sensing is conditioned on the current state.
optionExplanations.o4: The displayed measurement relation uses x_t, not x_(t−1).
